extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency SBIR/STTR program managers, SBA staff, policymakers, and other stakeholders involved in SBIR/STTR reporting and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and reporting requirements for federal agencies to document SBIR and STTR program activity, measure compliance with statutory minimum spending requirements, and report socioeconomic participation and award/obligation metrics in the SBA annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum spending requirements (FY22 percentages)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Small Business Act establishes minimum spending requirement percentages for each year. For FY22, the minimum spending requirement was 3.2% for the SBIR program and 0.45% for the STTR Program. Agencies are required to meet these minimum percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA determines whether Participating Agencies met the minimum by calculating the percentage of an agency’s extramural R/R&D obligations which funded SBIR/STTR awards and activities, compared to the agency’s total extramural R/R&D obligations for the fiscal year. The size of the SBIR/STTR Programs depends on the size of the extramural R/R&D budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory definition of extramural R/R&D (15 U.S.C. § 638(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: [T]he sum of the total obligations [for R/R&D] minus amounts obligated for such activities by employees of the agency in or through Government-owned, Government-operated facilities, except that for the Department of Energy it shall not include amounts obligated for atomic energy defense programs solely for weapons activities or for naval reactor programs, and except that for the Agency for International Development it shall not include amounts obligated solely for general institutional support of international research centers or for grants to foreign countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must apply this statutory definition when reporting extramural R/R&D obligations; note the DOE and AID exceptions spelled out in statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reporting of extramural R/R&D methodology (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Small Business Act requires Participating Agencies to report the methodology used to calculate their extramural R/R&D budget not later than four months after the date of the enactment of the agency’s appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodology disclosure is part of the annual reporting process to enable SBA evaluation of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NSF NCSES Survey extramural figures
rubrics_metrics.description: As prescribed in Section 10(h)(4)(iv) of the SBIR/STTR Policy Directive, Participating Agencies must report the total fiscal year extramural R/R&D obligations as reported to the U.S. National Science Foundation’s NCSES Survey of Federal Funds for Research and Development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because amounts reported to NCSES may differ from amounts reported to SBA, agencies are asked to provide a rationale for any variance; when provided, that explanation is included in the SBA report.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA compliance determination method
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA determines compliance based on agency-provided percent (Percent of SBIR/STTR Obligations as determined using agency-provided data) and by assessing the agency-provided data relative to extramural R/R&D obligations submitted to NSF NCSES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may appear compliant by agency-submitted data but be listed as 'Did Not Comply' (or another status) based on SBA’s independent assessment comparing to NCSES figures. Details of SBA’s validation process are provided in Section 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reporting fields for SBIR/STTR tables
rubrics_metrics.description: The report tables include standardized fields such as: Solicitations Released (#), New Proposals Received (#), New Awards (#), Selection Rate (%), Total Obligations ($), New Proposals/ New Awards/ New Obligations/ Total Obligations broken out by Phase (I, II, Admin, Phase III where applicable), Total Obligations for Research Institutions (STTR), Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) Provided by Agency ($), TABA Provided to Small Businesses in Award Obligations ($), Administrative Funding Pilot (AFPP) (3%) ($), DoD 1% CRP ($), Amount of Extramural R/R&D reported to SBA minus Exemptions ($), Percent of SBIR/STTR Obligations as determined using Agency-provided data (%), and SBA Assessment of Agency Compliance with Meeting Minimum Spending Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present both raw counts and dollar obligations and include breakdowns by phase and by socioeconomic group where applicable; agencies should report all fields to facilitate SBA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rate and awards/proposals timing note
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection Rate (%) is reported, but for some FY22 awards, agencies may have received proposals in prior fiscal years; as a result, the number of awards may be greater than the number of proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should annotate when awards derive from prior-year proposals to avoid misinterpretation of selection rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III exclusion from Total SBIR Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies cannot use SBIR/STTR funding for Phase III awards and these dollars are not part of Total SBIR Obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase III dollars listed in tables may include both SBIR and STTR program Phase III obligations but are explicitly excluded from the 'Total SBIR Obligations' calculations used to assess compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: TABA funds that were provided by the agency directly to the awardee through grant or contract are included in Phase I/Phase II obligation award amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When TABA funds are provided directly by the agency, these amounts are counted within award obligation totals and should be footnoted/explained in the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for data to match SBIR.gov and SBA upload (DoD/STTR specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA requires the data included in the report be a summation of individual awards uploaded to SBA by the DoD, and that this data match what is available on SBIR.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure consistency between award-level data on SBIR.gov and the aggregated annual report submissions to SBA; SBA validates and may flag discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting exemptions and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the annual report submission, each Participating Agency reports the total extramural R/R&D funds obligated that year along with exemptions and exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including exemptions/exclusions enables SBA’s evaluation of agency compliance with minimum spending requirements; agencies should clearly document what was excluded and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common accounting and transparency challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: A key challenge is identifying a common and transparent accounting of agency extramural R/R&D obligations for the year, given differences in agency reporting and definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should adopt transparent accounting practices aligned with statutory definitions and NCSES conventions to minimize variance and improve comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD reporting approach caveat (appropriations vs obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DoD continues to report extramural R/R&D budget appropriations rather than the actual amounts of funding obligated during the fiscal year; in this case SBA cannot validate whether DoD met the minimum spending requirements because the total extramural R/R&D obligations is unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must report actual obligations (not just appropriations) where statute requires obligations; otherwise SBA may list status as 'Unable to Determine.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/estimation of obligations during fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies cannot account for all obligations for SBIR/STTR awards or extramural R/R&D spending until the fiscal year is over; agencies must estimate these amounts and make minor adjustments when possible during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates should be documented and revised with final year-end data; SBA accounts for estimation uncertainty in its validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year/no-year funding cycles affect obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Several agencies have no‑year or two‑year funding cycles, which allows the agency to obligate those funds in future years; e.g., the DoD has a two-year funding cycle and much of DoD’s funding is obligated in the second year of availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA measures what was obligated in the current fiscal year regardless of the year the funds were set aside; agencies should indicate multi-year funding rules and expected obligation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socioeconomic participation reporting (WOSB, SDB, HUBZone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress directs the SBIR and STTR Programs to foster participation by women-owned small businesses (WOSB), socially and economically disadvantaged small businesses (SDB), and small businesses located in Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone). Agencies must summarize participation across these socioeconomic groups (number of proposals, awards, obligations, and percent shares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions for WOSB, SDB, and HUBZone are cited to the Policy Directive §3(ss), §3(ll), and 15 USC §632(p)(3); tables and charts should break out counts and obligations by these groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA assessment outcome categories
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA lists agency compliance outcomes such as 'Complied', 'Did Not Comply', 'Unable to Determine', and 'Various' in the assessment of meeting minimum spending requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA’s assessment combines agency-provided data with NCSES comparisons and other validation steps; agencies may receive different statuses depending on the validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual calculation of program funding share (agency vs NCSES)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report presents SBIR/STTR Program Funding as a share of agency-reported extramural R/R&D using: (1) calculation using extramural levels reported by Participating Agency to SBA and (2) calculation using extramural levels reported on NCSES Survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both calculations are shown to highlight variance; agencies should explain discrepancies when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR-specific reporting: obligations for research institutions and Phase 0 (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: For STTR tables, agencies report 'Total Obligations for Research Institutions' and the 'Total Obligations for Research Institutions (%)' and, where applicable, 'Obligations for "Phase 0" Programs (NIH only) ($)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STTR reporting requires differentiating obligations to research institutions and showing their percentage share of total STTR obligations; NIH must additionally report Phase 0 amounts where relevant.
